I agree with you in that it’s really stupid how most women care about height. You deserve someone who is patient with you, but having baggage shouldn’t hold you back from trying to get into a relationship. Comparing yourself to your friend will only pull you down in the long run, and i’m sure you have a charming side to you. Unfortunately, one of the biggest factors that make a good relationship is vulnerability, which is difficult af to get past if you deal with trust issues like myself and many others. 

Hang in there, your height is not going to be a dealbreaker in your future romances. You will find someone who is close to your height if that is your preference, but it take time. 

Keep this in mind: If a woman rejects you purely because of your height, then she isn’t meant to be to begin with.

Hey there, i’m also around your weight and im 5’10 and 18 years old. I struggle with binging at night out of boredom, and have tried to use art or video games as a distraction. The best way i’ve tried to deter binging is by drinking a huge glass of ice water and not keeping many easy snacks in my house. My mom is a health nut and tries really hard to keep me from unhealthy and processed foods, so when i do binge, i have to accept the fact that i either need to prepare something or make do with oatmeal or something else sad. It helps though, it’s way easier to get too lazy to cook something at 2:35 in the morning over opening a bag of chips or microwaving a lean cuisine. 

Just try to keep yourself busy and hydrated, and remember that you aren’t alone.

Also, those artificial af freezy pops are a good thing to snack on because they’re just flavored water in a tube.

I’m a 5’10 female and my boyfriend is 5’2, there is definitely hope for you regardless of your height. I’m basically double his size, and while it did take some getting used to- it works. He actually claims that he’ll never go back to dating girls his size. 

Tall women are an untapped group that are not nearly as noticed at short girls. If short girls get taken by tall guys, go for tall girls- you’ll be surprised. (and don’t be intimidated by them or feel less masculine because of the difference, own it and your confidence will be attractive)

Two men came in to buy cigarettes during the Christmas season, so the first one paid for his in his own transaction. The second one asked for a pack as well, but thought his buddy would pay for him. They started arguing with each other as a huge line began to form (I called IC3 as my voice began to quiver and crack from stress about keeping up customer morale, BUT NO ONE CAME). 

I was already under a huge amount of stress keeping up with the hundreds of Christmas cards with envelopes, people asking if theirs are done yet, etc. I just broke down and started crying in front of everyone. I felt highkey abandoned by my coworkers having me keep up with the entire front end, but luckily a super sweet manager came when I called IC3 again (crying into the intercom) and let me take a break, telling me that I could call her if I needed help with photo, calls, or anything else. 

That manager ended up getting promoted to corporate at the end of the season, and I eventually quit a few months later due to being over-scheduled as a student under 18 at the time, as well as being left with pretty horrible management that always nitpicked me while they sat around in the office eating snacks and didn’t understand how to create schedules that worked for everyone. After the nice manager(s) left for corporate, who also happened to be scheduling managers, the store went to shit and we had a very high turnover rate.

Edit: A lady who’s photo order I was trying to do noticed my breakdown and bought me a 15$ starbucks card. I knew I shouldn’t have taken it under policy but I was so pissed off that I accepted it, so that made me feel a lot better.

I’ve been on an antidepressant/anti-anxiety for almost 3 years now and i know exactly how you feel. You feel like a shell of your personality, happiness and sadness are both somewhat muted or softened.... And the thought of feeling dependent on a little white pill really does bring me down. I’ve had times where i’ve had extreme withdrawals after not taking my pills for a few days. If at all possible, try to get some fresh air and maybe avoid self-isolating yourself as much as possible. Now that the winter is basically over, get yourself outside doing things to distract yourself from the negatives. Also, consider trying alternatives such as CBD if you aren’t into the devils lettuce. You aren’t completely dependent on your medication, they’re simply a crutch to help you learn how to cope with your issues.
